**5B.7 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**
Overall judgment: **mixed, leaning no**. There is real evidence of evidence-based reform in macro stabilization, procurement, and health administration. But the larger 2024 pattern still shows denial of macro stress, blame-shifting, prestige/patronage-driven decisions, and a crisis style that preferred coercion over correction.

**Evidence For**
- [Bangladesh: Second Reviews Under the ECF/EFF and RSF Arrangements](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/186/article-A001-en.xml) | IMF | June 24, 2024 | IMF said program performance was broadly on track and highlighted exchange-rate realignment, a crawling peg, tighter monetary policy, and tax/subsidy reforms. This is the strongest evidence of evidence-based correction, though it was still largely a repair effort under external program pressure. `Question IDs: 5B.7, 5B.3`
- [Inclusion of govt procuring agencies in e-GP mandatory](https://bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1446.html) | Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority | March 6, 2024 | BPPA said e-GP was mandatory, that most agencies were already registered, and that online procurement improved transparency, efficiency, and competition. This is a concrete administrative reform consistent with policy based on evidence and process discipline. `Question IDs: 5B.7, 5B.6, 5B.4, 5B.5`
- [Advancing Healthcare Excellence: WHO's Role in Developing the First National Medical Education Strategy in Bangladesh!](https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh) | WHO Bangladesh | March 4, 2024 | The health ministry, with WHO support, launched work on Bangladesh’s first national medical education strategy to improve curriculum, accreditation, faculty development, and digital transformation. This is strong evidence of evidence-based sector policy. `Question IDs: 5B.7, 5B.6`
- [Bangladesh completes its second Joint External Evaluation of the International Health Regulations core capacities](https://www.who.int/southeastasia/news/detail/11-07-2024-2nd-jee-bn) | WHO | July 11, 2024 | Bangladesh completed its second JEE using the new eJEE platform, reviewing core health-security capacities and identifying priority actions. This is a real sign of technical review and correction, though in a narrow domain. `Question IDs: 5B.7, 5B.6`

**Evidence Against**
- [Financial Sector and Fiscal Policy Reforms Will Help Bangladesh Sustain Strong Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/02/financial-sector-and-fiscal-policy-reforms-will-help-bangladesh-sustain-strong-growth-despite-strong-growth-south-asia-r) | World Bank | April 2, 2024 | The Bank said growth was being disrupted by high inflation, a balance-of-payments deficit, financial-sector vulnerabilities, tight liquidity, import restrictions, and higher input costs. This undercuts the idea that policy had already corrected obvious macro mistakes. `Question IDs: 5B.7, 5B.3, 5B.4`
- [Factbox-Troubled Bangladesh's economy bogged down by high unemployment, inflation](https://m.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/factboxtroubled-bangladeshs-economy-bogged-down-by-high-unemployment-inflation-3561503?ampMode=1) | Reuters | August 8, 2024 | Reuters summarized widening external deficits, taka depreciation, falling reserves, inflation near 10%, and Bangladesh needing an IMF bailout. This is strong evidence against a clean evidence-based correction story in 2024. `Question IDs: 5B.7, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.6`
- [Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) | Reuters | July 22, 2024 | Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for deadly violence instead of pivoting to compromise or correction. This is direct scapegoating and denial rather than evidence-based adjustment. `Question IDs: 5B.7, 4B.1, 4B.8, 4B.9`
- [Bangladesh's crackdown on protests](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) | UN / OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity. That suggests a governing style that suppressed scrutiny rather than correcting mistakes through open evidence. `Question IDs: 5B.7, 4B.9, 4B.10`
- [Bangladesh's nuclear prestige illusion](https://www.thedailystar.net/opinion/views/news/bangladeshs-nuclear-prestige-illusion-3590666) | The Daily Star | April 20, 2024 | This opinion piece argued the second Rooppur plant push looked prestige-driven amid debt and inflation. This is weaker than the IMF/World Bank material, but it supports the inference that image politics competed with evidence-based economic judgment. `Question IDs: 5B.7, 5B.4, 5B.6`
- [Rooppur Power Plant was AL govt's white elephant: energy sector experts](https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/energy/rooppur-power-plant-was-al-govts-white-elephant-energy-sector-experts-958801) | TBS News | October 5, 2024 | Energy-sector experts described Rooppur as mismanaged and corruption-linked. If accepted, this points toward patronage and weak correction rather than disciplined, evidence-based capital allocation. `Question IDs: 5B.7, 5B.4, 5B.5, 5B.6`

**Search Gap**
I did not find strong direct evidence of Hasina personally running a systematic “learn-and-correct” process across the whole government in 2024. The best positives are mostly external-program reforms or narrow technical-sector reviews; the clearest negative evidence is the combination of macro stress, blame-shifting, and prestige-driven or patronage-prone decision-making.
